segment_text: 2.8 Transfer of Miltenyi Products. Bellicum shall have the right to transfer Miltenyi Product(s) purchased hereunder, or to request from Miltenyi, by notice in writing, that Miltenyi Deliver any Miltenyi Product(s) purchased hereunder to an Affiliate of Bellicum or a Subcontractor or Licensee of Bellicum Product designated by Bellicum, solely for the purpose of the Permitted Use, subject to the payment to Miltenyi of all additional expenses (if any) incurred by Miltenyi in connection with such provision and transfer of Miltenyi Product(s) to Bellicum's designee; and provided that in each case: (i) each Subcontractor or Licensee of Bellicum to whom Miltenyi Products are transferred shall be bound in writing by limitations and obligations that are consistent with the corresponding limitations and obligations imposed on Bellicum 8 Miltenyi Biotec-Bellicum Supply Agreement (Execution Copy, March 27, 2019) hereunder and under the Quality Agreement, as applicable; and (ii) notwithstanding the transfer of any Miltenyi Product purchased hereunder, Bellicum will nevertheless continue to remain fully and primarily responsible and liable to Miltenyi for payment of the Product Price and for the use of the Miltenyi Product by any Subcontractor and Licensee to whom a Miltenyi Product is transferred.

annotator_notes:
Sub-clause (ii)'s PAY half -- the segment's SECOND item, and THE FIRST LOCKED INSTANCE OF ONE section 8.8.4 PREDICATE CARRYING BOTH ITS LIMBS.

SEGMENT SHAPE. C04-033, 1,306 chars. BOTH GUARDS RUN BEFORE ANY ANNOTATION. F27 (splitter over-split): CLEAN -- zero redaction-induced splits, zero abbreviations, so the splitter's 2 fragments are both real (a heading and one long sentence). Section 8.7 (page furniture): the 74-char running header IS present, at [840:914], with page-number prefix 8 -- exactly as the 43-page measurement on C04-144 predicted.

THREE SPANS, ONE SENTENCE. main right [35:971] (item C04-12); sub-clause (i) [601:971] NOT_OBLIGATION_BEARING, inside the main span; sub-clause (ii) split at [982:1189] (item C04-13, the PAY half) and [1190:1306] (the ABSORB half, dispositioned out). The two ITEM spans are DISJOINT -- the gap is '; and (ii) ' -- so unlike E03-04/E03-05's nested pair section 4.1 cannot collide, and (ii) needed no section 8.3.1 shared-subject treatment because it carries its own subject and modal ('Bellicum will nevertheless continue to remain').

A CITATION OF MINE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN DROPPED. Drafting this segment I cited C04-05 as the precedent for mapping an agentless 'shall be bound' to ENSURE and for promoting Bellicum into the obligor slot. READING ITS COMMITTED SPAN FALSIFIES BOTH USES: C04-05 is "Bellicum shall use, and WILL CAUSE its Subcontractors and Licensees to use, Miltenyi Products in accordance with all Applicable Laws..." -- an ACTIVE construction with an explicit CAUSATIVE and obligor Bellicum as the STATED agent. It establishes ENSURE for "will cause X to do Y", a named-agent causative; it says nothing about an agentless 'X shall be bound'. The reviewer's standing instruction to verify a precedent's span before citing it is what caught this.

AND THE PROMOTION I PROPOSED CONTRADICTED MY OWN REASONING FROM FOUR SEGMENTS EARLIER. I argued obligor ABSENT for C10-03's agentless passive on section 3.5.3's grounds, then proposed promoting Bellicum here from a possessive ('of Bellicum') and a comparison phrase ('imposed on Bellicum') -- the exact inference section 3.5.3's own C04-087 case forbids ("a possessive on a place is not a duty-bearer; reading one as the obligor is section 3.5's forbidden inference"). Recorded because the inconsistency is the useful part: the rule was applied correctly when the span had no plausible candidate and incorrectly when a party name happened to be nearby.

THE SPLIT IS THE RULING, AND SECTION 8.8.4's HOLDING IS WHAT DECIDES IT: THE COMPLEMENT DECIDES, NOT THE CONSTRUCTION. The predicate "Bellicum will nevertheless continue to remain fully and primarily responsible and liable to Miltenyi" governs TWO coordinated complements that fall on OPPOSITE sides of section 8.8.4's own test:
    "for payment of the Product Price" -- an ACT NOMINALISATION, which section 8.8.4's head-noun proxy puts on the RENDER side. Obligation-bearing. THIS ITEM.
    "and for the use of the Miltenyi Product by any Subcontractor and Licensee to whom a Miltenyi Product is transferred" -- ANOTHER PERSON'S CONDUCT, section 8.8.4's ABSORB limb (c). NOT_OBLIGATION_BEARING; dispositioned out in the segment file.
  Section 8.8.4 records that this split can occur inside one sentence and names C04-088 as repeating the C03-016/C03-024 pair "inside one segment" -- but C04-088 IS NOT A LOCKED ITEM, checked rather than assumed, so no adjudicated instance of ONE predicate carrying BOTH limbs across a coordinated complement existed before this. RULED AS CASE-LAW, NO AMENDMENT: section 8.8.4's rule already decides it; what is new is the configuration, not the test.

  TWO READINGS WERE DRAFTED AND REJECTED, recorded because the first is tempting. (1) ABSORB GOVERNS THE WHOLE PREDICATE -- the clause's work is retaining liability NOTWITHSTANDING a transfer, and "continue to remain fully and primarily responsible AND LIABLE" is C03-024's "shall remain liable for" almost verbatim, which section 8.8.4 rules is the ABSORB paradigm. REJECTED: it lets the VERB PAIR override the COMPLEMENT, which inverts section 8.8.4's central holding. (2) SPLIT INTO TWO ITEMS, the ABSORB half becoming its own. REJECTED: an ABSORB half is NOT a clause -- that is what NOT_OBLIGATION_BEARING means -- and counting it would have put the segment at 4 and over section 2's band.

SECTION 4.3.1 STEP 1 WAS RUN AGAINST EVERY LOCKED C04 ITEM BEFORE DRAFTING, and this is not a restatement of any of them. The nearest in economic substance is C04-01 (Bellicum reimbursing Miltenyi for third-party royalties), which differs on THREE scored fields: action REIMBURSE vs PAY, object_class third_party_royalties vs product_price, and a different segment. C04-02's 'payment_responsibility' is a NEGOTIATE item about WHO WILL OWE payment, not a duty to pay. Step 1 requires every scored field identical. SET-LEVEL FACT RECORDED BECAUSE A READER MIGHT ASSUME OTHERWISE: PAY is a taxonomy member but appears in NO locked C04 item, so this is the document's first -- across the whole set PAY appears only on C02-04 and C14-06.

MODALITY MUST. "will" states a party's undertaking, not a future fact about the agreement -- section 3.2's will-ambiguity rule, the undertaking side.

SPAN IS THE MINIMAL SUBSTRING STATING THE COMPLETE OBLIGATION, section 3.1: [982:1189], ending at "for payment of the Product Price" and deliberately EXCLUDING the ABSORB complement at [1190:1306]. Including it would extend the span past the duty for no gain and would put a NOT_OBLIGATION_BEARING clause inside an item's span unnecessarily -- unlike C14-02 and C14-06, where a shared subject made that unavoidable.

ACTION PAY, a literal taxonomy member; the complement names the payment and the payee. Singleton accept-set: REIMBURSE was CONSIDERED AND DECLINED, because reimbursing is repaying a cost another party bore, and the Product Price is Bellicum's own primary obligation, not a reimbursement -- which is also exactly what distinguishes this item from C04-01.

OBLIGOR "Bellicum", OBLIGEE "Miltenyi" -- both named in-span ("liable TO MILTENYI for payment") and BOTH RESOLVE against evals/registry/C04.json, verified by reading it.

UNDERSPECIFIED FALSE, missing_fields EMPTY. Section 3.9's four triggers checked individually: both parties resolve; no DateRef; no TriggerRef; no bd duration. The second batch-5 item for which this is true, after C04-11.

OBJECT_CLASS 'product_price'. Head noun of the object phrase ("payment of the Product Price") is "price", carried as the head-only member section 3.6's v0.58 rule requires. SECTION 3.6.1 CLEAR: no member restates PAY or either party. SECTION 3.6.2 IS THE LIVE CHECK HERE AND IT CLEARS: 'payment' IS the nominal of PAY, so 'payment' was DELIBERATELY NOT AUTHORED as a member -- it would be the cognate-object residue that collapses clauses 2 and 5, exactly C22-01's NOTIFY/notice problem. 'price' and 'product_price' carry the object without restating the act.

CONDITIONS EMPTY. "notwithstanding the transfer of any Miltenyi Product purchased hereunder" is a CONCESSIVE, not a circumstance: section 3.8.2's removal test leaves the duty unchanged -- Bellicum owes the Product Price whether or not a transfer occurs. It says the duty SURVIVES a transfer, which is the opposite of gating it.

TEMPORAL NULL -- cell (c): no timing on the duty.

PROVENANCE. As for C04-12: pool rebuild gate, byte-for-byte match against draw.json, both guards run.
